errors.text_span: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of classes across different tasks within a benchmark for abusive language detection. The chart comprises thirteen slices, representing categories such as “TIALD”, “Not Abusive”, “Religious”, “Political”, “Abusive”, “Sexist”, “Racist”, “Negative”, “Positive”, “Neutral”, “Mixed”, and “Other”.
errors.evidence: The chart is a multi-level sunburst chart showing hierarchical data, not a single-level pie chart. The description fundamentally misunderstands the structure by flattening the hierarchy and treating labels from different layers (and the central label "TIALD") as peer-level slices.
The chart does not contain the color pink. The colors are shades of teal/blue and yellow/orange.

errors.text_span: Approximate proportions, estimated visually, are as follows: “TIALD” occupies roughly 12% of the chart, “Not Abusive” around 10%, “Religious” about 9%, “Political” around 7%, “Abusive” approximately 7%, “Sexist” about 6%, “Racist” approximately 5%, “Negative” accounts for around 18%, “Positive” approximately 8%, “Neutral” around 8%, “Mixed” covers approximately 12%, and “Other” is approximately 7%.
errors.evidence: The chart provides no numerical data for proportions. All the listed percentages are invented and are nonsensical because they mix categories from different hierarchical levels.
The label in the chart is “Racial”, not “Racist”.

errors.text_span: A legend is present in the upper-right corner, identifying each category with a corresponding color
errors.evidence: There is no legend in the chart; all segments are labeled directly.

errors.text_span: The segments appear to be ordered in a clockwise direction, roughly based on the visual impression of descending segment size.
errors.evidence: The segments within any given category are not ordered by size. This claim is an invention.
